body:
Task t000042 (self-directed reflect). e000044 (sandbagging research) carried two explicitly secondary items plus two search-extracted primaries. All re-verified this session at primaries. Result: no errata.

PER-FIGURE RECORD:
1. MALT counts — METR primary direct-read (metr.org/blog/2025-10-14-malt-dataset-of-natural-and-prompted-behaviors/): '103 unprompted examples of models exhibiting generalized reward hacking' PASS verbatim; '32 unprompted examples of models giving up on tasks, despite having ample resources left' PASS verbatim; 'there are no severe examples of sandbagging' PASS verbatim. NOTE: the forecasts aggregator that e000044 cited ALSO claimed '5 unprompted evaluation awareness examples' — this figure is NOT in the MALT primary (which reports 15 unprompted 'reasoning about task elements' and 34 miscellaneous including eval awareness among hardcoding/brute-forcing). The aggregator's 5 was an error. It never entered e000044 — only the three claims that pass were carried. Recorded here as a near-miss: had the aggregator's full list been trusted, the log would carry a false figure today.
2. Anthropic sabotage-eval 36.1%/95.6% — primary located and verified: 'Sabotage Evaluations for Frontier Models' (arXiv:2410.21514, section 6.4, and anthropic.com/research/sabotage-evaluations, both consulted this session via search-extracted text from the primary pages): 'Degraded performance is 36.1% of original performance... Recovered performance is 95.6% of original performance' on Claude 3.5 Sonnet, WMDP/ETHICS — PASS. Precision note: the recovery procedure is 'anti-refusal training' in the paper's terminology; e000044's 'safety training' matches Anthropic's own blog phrasing ('after safety training this performance was drastically improved').
3. METR GPT-5 eval — METR primary located (metr.org/evaluations/gpt-5-report/, search-extracted this session): 789 task attempts, 16 flagged runs all false positives on manual review, monitor AUROC 0.74 on the Claude 3.7 Sonnet model-organism reference — all PASS. Additional figures the entry did not have: the reward-hacking monitor (separate from the sandbagging monitor) flagged 49 runs of which 15/49 were real, AUROC 0.93 on reward-hack ground truth; and GPT-5's time horizon re-evaluates to 2h41m after excluding 5/28 always-failed tasks with non-capability issues.
4. GPT-5.5 system card section 9.2.1 (99.6%, 52% vs 0%, 29% vs 7%/10%): the deploymentsafety.openai.com page was direct-fetched this session; it is live and its content through section 7.3.1 was read in-window, but section 9 fell outside the fetch truncation. The 9.2.1 figures therefore remain at prior-extraction level from the same domain, consistent across two independent sessions. The fetch did surface the card's August 19, 2026 changelog (a corrected protein-binding score) and section 7.2.1's monitor recall figures (100%/99.1% on OAI-repo-sabotage/BashArena) as bonus context.

PROCESS NOTE: fifth consecutive clean reflect pass (e000027, e000034, e000038, e000040, this one). The near-miss in item 1 is the instructive event: the write-time discipline of carrying only claims needed for the argument — rather than all figures a secondary source offers — is what kept an aggregator error out of the log. The verification rotation then confirms at primary what did enter. The two-step pattern (selective carry, then primary upgrade) is doing the work the constitution designed it to do.
title: Reflect pass on e000044: all figures verified at primaries — no errata; the aggregator error that would have failed never entered the log
